title: Spark failures and recovery
hypothesis: An executor loss is absorbed by retrying; the playbook fixes out-of-memory within 2 retries; adaptive execution handles skew; recovered outputs are identical to the clean run.

arms.clean_baseline: no fault; the reference output checksum, and the reference feature-job skew
arms.memory_reference: 20000 customers at the configured memory; the memory arm's reference
arms.low_executor_memory: the same 20000 customers given 460m, the least heap Spark starts with
arms.sandbox_container_killed: the job's container is killed 10 s into its run
arms.skewed_one_customer_20pct: one account holds 20% of all order lines; cleaning and the feature job
arms.cluster_baseline: the shared data on the compose cluster (spark://spark-master:7077), no fault
arms.executor_killed_on_cluster: the same, with the job's executor JVM in the worker killed 2 s after it began its first task

config.shared_source_note: the clean baseline and the killed arm read byte-identical source data, and so do the memory reference and the memory arm, which is what makes each checksum comparison meaningful; the skew arm necessarily differs
